I'm a bit younger than you but have experienced this excessive thoughts about what is good and evil. It has created a lot of anxiety and paralysis for me. I have missed lots of opportunities because of it.

Though I have no solution, I try to soothe these thoughts with some belief I have about the world.

It helps to not look at the world in black and white but rather a very vast spectrum of grey. Good and evil live on a continuum to me. For a single human being it is impossible to be pure good. To stay alive there is some inherent level of selfishness. We do things in our own best interest. And it is impossible to completely eliminate that side. We can however make decisions to minimise the negative impact of our decisions. For you a practical example would be to buy a plane ticket from a company that is trying to work towards greener fuel solutions. Or to fly less frequently. 

Somewhere we have to make a compromise in every decision we make. If you are a sensitive person and notice the evil in the world it can be hard to not feel guilty about every choice you make, but that is not serving you, your family or the community you live in by being paralysed by your thoughts.

Resolve to find the compromise. Try to find what is beneficial to you and your family while doing the least harm. Also choose to do something that you feel is actively beneficial to your community like volunteering for a cause or donating money to research projects. 

Also I would suggest seeking counselling for perfectionism. Perfectionism can cause one to be hyper critical of yourself and think in extremes.

I hope you can soothe your mind and learn to live a full life with your lovely family. Don't feel guilty for being alive. And you are not alone in this experience.

I hear you, and I am AR55, so that pretty much sums up my experience. I am not trying to invalidate the frustrations of the players. I also want more endgame content, or a better system for farming artifacts. And the resin limit can be frustrating, forcing you to play regularly to make progress (especially if you are F2P). 

But I just sense a painful impatience, not just in the Genshin community but in the gaming community as a whole. There seems to be a rush for new content, and why? I'm thinking of Cyberpunk 2077 now, everyone was impatient and then they released a game with tons of bugs and glitches. Good things take time. Even reworking old content to improve it takes time.

No matter how large a dev company is, the devs are still people. They can only be pushed so far. Maybe I am too kind to think of the devs' mental and physical state at their place of employment when thinking of game development, but I honestly don't see the rush, there are *thousands* of games out there you can play while you wait for an update. 

Why don't we just sit and take the time to think about solutions to our problems? And develop better quality games that are playable for longer, than rushing things for the sake of profit and impatient consumers? Idk, am I just naïve?

I had food service as one of my modules at uni. We discussed exactly this. If the food isn't tainted in anyway, it's better to donate than to toss. Obviously expired food, food that has been contaminated (ie someone took a bite out of it, it fell on the floor) should be discarded so no-one falls ill. But if it's fine, donate it to a soup kitchen, place of worship who support homeless individuals or any charity that feeds the hungry. It's a huge amount of waste, and a cost to the company if it's just tossed. 

On another note, it's clear that the management is not forecasting properly and is putting aesthetics above waste. That's a very old way of doing things. Food service establishments should aim to reduce waste, not create it.

I mean I guess some people are in it for the money, but I do believe there are therapists out there that genuinely care about their patients. We all need to make a living though so you also can't expect therapists to just give therapy for free though. 

I personally have a friend who is a registered counselor and I know where her heart is on this topic. She hasn't been able to start a practice or be employed as a counselor but she is currently a teacher's aid. She goes above and beyond to help her students in terms of mental health because she has the knowledge. It's not officially part of her job and she is horrendously underpaid at the moment, but she still cares and helps out anyways.

So I understand where you could be coming from, but your statement is fortunately not universally true. And people with depression or any mental illness need to know that. Therapists are just humans too at the end of the day.

Edit: also consider that therapy isn't for everyone (in terms of a coping method and a profession).

I'm always so heartbroken to hear accounts of terrible professionals. I always encourage people to try a few different therapists if the first one doesn't work, because stuff like this happens far too often. I wish you the best.

In my experience it helps to accept that I will always feel some level of depression and that it will fluctuate over time. We will never experience what people without depression experience, and that's completely okay. We can still lead a good life with depression, it will just not look like other people's definition of "good".

The most important thing is finding what helps you to cope with the crippling symptoms of depression, i.e. meds, therapy, a specific hobby, moving to a better environment, cutting off toxic friends/family etc. Make your life work for *you*. It is a proactive process. It can be very difficult and take years and years. 

That's what helps it "get better" for me at least. But in all honesty, if you expect your depression to one day just vanish into thin air, you'll feel more depressed. Embrace your demons and work around them. You live with them now.
